# yantra (CLI)

> The command-line client, and the daemon's first client. It renders and chooses exit codes; every
> decision about what is true belongs to `yantra-core` (ADR-0005). It calls that crate in-process
> today and becomes an HTTP client of `yantrad` later — a change of *where* the work is called from,
> not *what* it does. One file, `src/main.rs`.

## Commands

- `yantra new <workspace> --machine M --repo P [--startup CMD]`: write a workspace file. Refuses to overwrite one that exists.
- `yantra edit <workspace> [--machine M] [--repo P] [--startup CMD | --no-startup]`: change one that already does. **Refuses to change `machine` while a session is open on the one it would leave** — that session would stay where nothing looks for it (I-30). Needs at least one field.
- `yantra repair <workspace>`: replace a workspace file that will not load, with bytes read from stdin. The one write that composes nothing ([ADR-0020](../../docs/adr/0020-a-raw-write-only-from-broken-to-valid.md)), and bounded on both sides: it refuses a file that already loads, and it refuses bytes that still will not, naming the next error. So it can move a file from broken to valid and nowhere else — `edit` cannot reach one at all, since `update` loads before it writes. The read half is `cat`: every refusal already prints the path, and `ls workspaces` prints it under the table. It exists because `$EDITOR` writes the file too and says nothing about whether the repair worked.
- `yantra up <workspace> [--agent claude]`: open the workspace's tmux session, optionally launching Claude Code in it. Running it twice attaches rather than duplicating.
- `yantra resume <workspace>`: put the agent back on the conversation it left off, in the pane it died in. Refuses when the pane holds something it did not start.
- `yantra logs <workspace> [-n N]`: the last N turns of the agent's transcript, plus how long since anything was written.
- `yantra status <workspace>`: running, finished, stopped, crashed, killed — or unclear, with the reason.
- `yantra tokens <workspace>`: what the session has spent — input, output, cache write, cache read, each as Claude Code recorded it ([tokens.rs](../yantra-core/src/tokens.rs)), then in dollars per model at [price.rs](../yantra-core/src/price.rs)'s table. The counts do not add to a fifth number, so money is the only total, and **the day the table was true is printed on the same line as the figure** — the transcript carries no rate, so a written-down one is what stands between the count and the cost. A model the table does not carry is shown unpriced rather than free, and a session with a fast-mode response reports tokens and no money at all. A verb of its own rather than a line in `status`, because reading the whole transcript is the wrong price for a liveness check that scripts run in a loop.
- `yantra down <workspace>`: stop the session, reporting how the agent ended.
- `yantra rm <workspace> [--force]`: delete the workspace file. Refuses while its machine still holds the session, and refuses when the machine cannot be asked (R-23) — deleting the file would leave the session where nothing looks for it, and `down`/`resume`/`status`/`logs` would each report it absent (I-30). `--force` skips asking rather than ignoring the answer. Deleting what is already gone exits **0**.
- `yantra kill <machine> <session>`: stop a tmux session by machine and name — the sessions `ls sessions` finds that no workspace claims, which `down` cannot reach. Not `down`: there is no agent ending to read, so it only stops it. Prints *killed* or *no session*, and exits **0** for both (I-30).
- `yantra probe <machine> <path>`: ask a machine whether a directory is there and what git `origin` it holds, in one round trip. Exit **0** only when it exists, so `yantra probe m /p && yantra new …` reads the way it looks; a machine that could not be asked also exits 1, with the reason on stderr (R-23). This is what lets a form select rather than fill (Y-185) — `up` asks the same question today, but only after the workspace file exists.
- `yantra ls machines`: the tailnet, advisory only.
- `yantra ls sessions`: tmux sessions on every machine a workspace names or the tailnet offers (Y-176). Exit 1 if any machine was unreachable — the table still prints, so a caller can tell the answer is partial.
- `yantra ls attention`: issues assigned to you, pull requests waiting on your review, and the unread notification count — read through `gh`, so Yantra holds no GitHub token ([R13](../../docs/research/13-dashboard-revamp-and-github.md) §2.2). Exit 1 when `gh` is absent, logged out or cannot reach GitHub, each said by name; an empty inbox is exit 0, because nothing waiting is an answer.
- `yantra notify <message> [--title T] [--priority 1-5]`: publish to the relay `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` names, with `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN` if the topic is protected (Y-147). The body is sent as written — the relay is a general channel and the fleet notifier is only its other caller — and the one command that proves topic, token and egress from a box with no screen. Every refusal names the variable that would change it and neither the token nor the URL is ever printed.
- `yantra doctor [machine] [--json]`: what each machine can and cannot do — the nine checks in [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md), each present, absent or unknown, for every machine a workspace names or for the one named. **It changes nothing** and there is no `--fix`. Exit 0 only when every check is present, so an installer can loop on it; `--json` is the shape an installer and an agent read, and `the_json_shape_is_pinned` is its contract.
- `yantra fix-terminfo <machine>`: teach a machine the terminal you are sitting at.
- `yantra ssh-identity`: prepare this account's `~/.ssh` — a key, and a `Host` block per machine a workspace names — and print the public key to place in each `authorized_keys` ([D2 §2](../../docs/design/02-setup.md)). Idempotent, and **invoked rather than automatic**: whether generating the keypair is Yantra's job at all is still the owner's to confirm. It writes no `known_hosts`, because [yantra-core's `ssh`](../yantra-core/src/ssh.rs) already gives every connection its own.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): the whole crate. Clap definitions at the top, one `async fn` per command, then the `render_*` and `describe` helpers, then tests.
